title: Profit, loss and return
blurb: A short mission: find out if Asha's samosa stall made money, and why a fall hurts more than a rise helps.
t1.title: Meet Asha's stall
t1.hook: Asha buys 50 samosas for {buy} and sells them all for {sell}. Your mission: work out if she did well.
t1.define: **Profit** is what you keep after paying your costs. If you end up with less, that is a **loss**.
t1.analogy: Think of a tea stall. You spend {buy} on supplies. Customers pay {sell}. The extra money is your profit.
q1.prompt: Asha sold all her samosas for {sell}. She paid {buy} for them. What is her profit? Type a number in rupees.
q1.hint: Profit = what she sold for minus what she paid.
q2.prompt: Which word means ending up with LESS money than you started with?
q2.hint: Think about the opposite of profit.
q2.explain: Ending up with less money is a loss.
t2.title: Return: comparing fairly
t2.define: **Return** is profit as a percentage of what you put in. It lets you compare small and big amounts fairly.
t2.steps.2: Return = profit ÷ what you paid, shown as a percentage
q3.prompt: What is Asha's return on her samosas? Type a percentage.
q3.hint: Divide her profit ({profit1}) by what she paid ({buy}). Then write it as a percentage.
q4.prompt: Asha gains {g1} on {b1}. Imran gains {g2} on {b2}. Who had the higher return?
q4.opt.b: Imran, because he gained more rupees
q4.hint: Return compares the gain to the amount put in. Work out each percentage.
q4.explain: Asha earned {r1} and Imran earned {r2}. Imran made more rupees, but on a much bigger amount.
t3.title: A bad day
t3.steps.1: A bad day: Asha sells everything for just {lowSell}.
t3.steps.2: She still paid {buy}, so she ends up with less than she started with.
t3.steps.3: A profit below zero is a loss. We write it with a minus sign.
t3.paper: A gain or loss on something you still hold is a **paper** gain or loss. It becomes **realised** only when you sell.
q5.prompt: On the bad day she sells for {lowSell}. What is her profit? Use a minus sign for a loss.
q5.hint: Selling price minus what she paid. The answer is below zero.
q5.explain: {lowSell} minus {buy} is {loss1}. The minus sign means a loss.
q6.prompt: What is her return on the bad day? Type a percentage with a minus sign.
q6.hint: Divide the loss by what she paid, then write it as a percentage.
q7.prompt: Ravi's shares are now worth {paperLoss} less than he paid. He has not sold them. What is this loss called?
q7.hint: Read the note above. Has he sold the shares?
q7.explain: He still holds the shares, so the loss is only on paper. It becomes realised if he sells.
t4.title: Lab: falls and rises
t4.explore: Open the lab. Drag the slider to try different falls, then answer the questions below.
q8.prompt: In the lab, drag the fall to {fall}. What rise do you need to get back to the start? Type a percentage.
q8.hint: Use the slider. Read the big number at the bottom.
q8.explain: After a fall of {fall} you hold {afterFall}. To get {startAmt} back, it must double: a rise of {needGain}.
q9.prompt: Now drag the fall to {fall2}. What rise do you need? Type a percentage.
q9.hint: Use the same slider. Watch how fast the big number grows.
q9.explain: After a fall of {fall2} you need a rise of {needGain2}. Big falls are very hard to win back.
q10.prompt: A price falls by {fall}, then rises by {fall}. Where does it end up compared with the start?
q10.fb.a: It feels even, but the rise is taken from the smaller amount, so it adds back less than you lost.
q10.hint: Try {startAmt} in the lab. Compare the grey bar with the yellow bar.
q10.explain: {startAmt} falls to {afterFall}, then rises to {afterRise}. That is 25% below the start.
t5.title: Rupees or percent?
t5.tradeoff: Percentages and rupees tell different stories. A big percentage on a small amount can be fewer rupees than a small percentage on a big amount. Always check both.
t5.mistake: Many people think a fall of {fall} and a rise of {fall} cancel out. They do not. Remember the lab: you need a bigger rise to win it back.
q11.prompt: How many rupees is a gain of {bigPct} on {bigBase}? Type a number.
q12.prompt: Which gain is more in rupees: {bigPct} on {bigBase}, or {smallPct} on {smallBase}?
q12.hint: Work out both in rupees. The bigger percentage is not always the bigger gain.
t6.title: Challenge
t6.formula: Return = (value now - value you paid) ÷ value you paid. To recover from a fall of x, you need a rise of x ÷ (1 - x).
q13.prompt: Challenge: a share falls by {fall3}. What rise gets it back to the start? Type a percentage.
q13.hint: After the fall you hold 80 out of every 100. How much more do you need on top of 80?
q13.explain: You need 20 more on top of 80. That is a rise of {needGain3}.
glossary.profit.def: Money left after paying all your costs.
glossary.loss.def: When you end up with less money than you started with.
glossary.return.def: Profit as a percentage of the money you put in.
glossary.paper_gain.def: A gain or loss on something you still hold and have not sold.
glossary.realised.def: A gain or loss that is locked in because you sold.
